name: new_configuration_activates_itself
why: SOLIDWORKS activates the configuration just created without anybody asking it to. It is not written anywhere in the call, and it changes everything that comes after: the faces, the volume, the mass and the properties the state tells are those of THAT variant. Whoever creates two configurations and then draws believes they are working on the first and is working on the last.
_why_the_comparison_with_the_state: The operation says «active_now». The state of the document is read by another part of the code: if the two lines diverged, one of the two would be lying, and this case is the only place where it would show.

expect.why: TWO, AND NOT ONE. A part just born from the template of this company already has two real configurations -- «Default<A macchina>» and «Default<Saldato>», the pair of the weldments. The number one starts from is not the one it would be natural to write, and this line cost a red: the count is here on purpose, instead of being taken for granted. The NAMES cannot be written -- «A macchina» and «Saldato» are localised, and a case that wrote them would be green on this installation and red on the next.

`GetConfigurationCount()` and `GetConfigurationNames()` are two different calls, and here they answer the same number. It is written because the day they did not match, that would be the fact to know: they would be two lists of the same thing that do not agree.
it is the line the entry asked for: «a configuration created and activated changes the active state read from DocumentState»
the new configuration is born as a copy of the one before: if the volume changed, the variant would no longer be the same part
the second dislodges the first, and this too without anybody having asked for it
